summary: Dennis Hirota is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at UC Berkeley (BA 1967, MA 1969) and Nagoya University (PhD 1996). He worked at Hongwanji International Center (~1974–1994) and was a professor at Ryukoku University (~1994–2017).

Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He served on the faculty at Smith College, where he was Professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies (attested 1987–1989) and taught religion (attested 2000).

Denzaburo Yoshizawa (1924–2003) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1946–1949). He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1957–1987) and Iryo Sosei University (~1987–1997).

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, later serving as co-director of East Carolina University's Religious Studies Program (attested 2010).

Dermot Killingley is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS. He held posts at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and Newcastle University (~1970–2000), also serving as visiting professor at the University of Vienna (2008).

Dermott Walsh is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (BA 2003), Leiden University (MA 2009), and completed his PhD in 2018 at the University of California, Los Angeles, under William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910) and as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917).
Dewei Zhang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of British Columbia under the supervision of Jinhua Chen (attested 2010).

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906–1987) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under Gaton Ngawang Lekpa, Ngawang Nyima, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960–1972).

Dharmananda Kosambi (1876–1947) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Harvard in 1926 and held posts at the University of Calcutta (~1906–1908), Harvard University (~1910–1931), Gujarat University (~1920–1925), and Saint Petersburg State University (~1929–1930).

Dhirendra Mohan Datta (1898–1974) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at the University of Calcutta. He held appointments at Patna College (1928) and the University of Minnesota (1951–1952).
Dhirendra Sharma (1932–2022) was a scholar in the fields of philosophy and Indology who studied under Surendra Sharma and David Friedman.

Dhivan Thomas Jones is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied under Richard Gombrich and Margaret Cone. He has held teaching posts at the Open University (attested 2017) and the University of Chester (2019).
Di Jiang is a scholar in linguistics, computational fields, and Tibetology. He has held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and as a professor at Jiangsu Normal University.
Di Luo is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Southern California under the supervision of Sonya S. Lee (attested 2016).
Diana L. Eck is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, SOAS, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She has served as a professor at Harvard University from ~1976.

Diana Lange is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet, and Humboldt universities and EPHE, she held posts at TU Berlin, Leipzig, Zurich, Hamburg, and was named Professorin at Humboldt University in 2025.

Diane A. Lichtenstein completed her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. She held positions as Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art (attested 2005).

Diane Elizabeth Riggs is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who earned her PhD at UCLA under William M. Bodiford. She held posts at Pepperdine University, Kenyon College (attested 2010), and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).
Diane L. Howard is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied as a graduate student at McMaster University under the supervision of Graeme MacQueen (attested 1982).
